contributions.text: Proposes Saethtior, a Java test generator that selects inputs by the mutants they kill, targeting surviving mutants.
contributions.quote: First, a generator that targets surviving mutants.

contributions.text: Adds a check that reruns each newly generated test to identify flaky tests, which are reported rather than discarded.
contributions.quote: Second, a check that reruns each new test to find flaky ones.

contributions.text: Reports an evaluation on 30 open-source Java projects.
contributions.quote: Third, an evaluation on 30 open-source projects.

evaluation.text: Seeded faults from a different mutation tool than the guidance tool are compared against a random baseline under the same ten-minute budget on 30 projects. Reports 18 percent more faults found and 37 of 42 flaky tests confirmed by hand.
evaluation.quote: Saethtior found 18 percent more seeded faults than the baseline.

prior_work.text: Positions search-based generation as optimizing coverage without mutants, and cites mutation-analysis studies as motivation for using mutants as a fault proxy. Flaky-test work is cited as measuring prevalence, whereas this paper detects flaky tests during generation.
prior_work.quote: Studies of mutation analysis [2] motivate our use of mutants.

closest_cited_work.text: The paper's genetic-algorithm search for killing inputs follows the style of this search-based unit test generation work.
closest_cited_work.quote: using a genetic algorithm in the style of earlier work [1]
